solve: Fitted by least squares (an unpitched camera, as photo_match draws it) to five points read off the scan at 1920 x 1407 px against the GLB's footprint frame (u along the front, the west gable the +u end; v toward the river): the farmstead's largest house is taken as the Kinzie house seen end-on from the east, its east gable toward the eye and its ridge running away to the right, which is how a house whose ridge runs along the river reads from up or down the river. Points: the east gable's apex (1462, 680), the heads of the near and far stacks (1469, 672; 1492, 677), the gable's back eave corner (1499, 712) and the front slope's eave over the piazza (1420, 712). The house is about 80 px wide on the scan, so the principal point is held at the plate's middle and its horizon (972, 700: the far prairie's line at the vanishing river) and the focal at 1600 px, as on the Lossing and Cram cameras. Eye (-160.66, -71.55) at 3.41 m, heading 47.85 degrees, rms 4.88 px: about 175 m east-north-east of the house, low, looking up the river to the south-west, which puts the fort's site, about 100 m south of the house, to the left of it as the plate draws the second fort. With the focal and principal free the fit runs to a 150 px lens 12 m from the house (rms 2.25 px), a camera no reading of the plate supports; five points cannot hold seven unknowns.
